lines.trans: Kostya, what are you doing right now?
I am standing and polishing glasses.
And I want to stay at your place today.
At my place? Did someone kick you out?
No, it is time for us to take the next step.
Do you want to get married?
Kostik, you are so funny!
We will simply spend this evening together.
And we will not tell anyone anything?

words.gram: dative singular; double negation with нельзя
genitive (with не); г is said like в

lines.trans: This will be our little secret.
Great, that sounds very logical.
I will quickly buy beautiful candles.
Good, make this evening magical!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'тирать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to rub'.

examples.trans: I am standing and polishing glasses.

examples.text: Я уже целый час стою и натираю бокалы до блеска.
examples.trans: I have been standing and polishing wineglasses to a shine for a whole hour.

examples.text: Повар быстро натирает твёрдый сыр на мелкой тёрке.
examples.trans: The cook quickly grates hard cheese on a fine grater.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wine glass, champagne flute, goblet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll drink from our wine glasses.
She raised a glass of champagne.

examples.text: Ничего страшного! Мы из наших бокалов выпьем.
examples.trans: No problem! We'll drink from our wine glasses.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left
Secondary conversational sense ('to stay') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('someone') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

выгнать.gloss: to kick out, to evict, to drive out

meanings.en: to kick out, to drive out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to kick out', forming an aspectual pair with 'выгонять'.

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

examples.text: Значит, меня не выгонят со службы?
examples.trans: Does that mean I won't be fired from service?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: в следующий раз = next time; следующий! = next, please!

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

examples.text: Так, с этим блюдом закончили, кто у нас следующий в очереди?
examples.trans: All right, we finished with this dish, who is next in line for us?

meanings.note: movement by foot or figurative action

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом соперника.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the rival.

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом кандидата.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the candidate.

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get out (be released)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: used with verbs like выходить for marriage of a woman

examples.trans: He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

examples.text: Она вышла замуж в прошлом году.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешной'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('funny, ridiculous').
Secondary conversational sense ('ridiculous, laughable') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты такой смешной, Тузик! Кто такой сладкий?
examples.trans: You're so funny, Tuzik! Who's so sweet?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'вести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to spend', forming an aspectual pair with 'проводить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to lead, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We spent the evening at home.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
Secondary conversational sense ('party, evening event') (e.g. a school evening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'together'.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
Borrowed via French 'secret' from Latin 'secretum' (something set apart or hidden).

examples.trans: These are our little men's secrets!

examples.text: А вы кем работаете, если не секрет?
examples.trans: And what do you do, if it is not a secret?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'excellently'.
Secondary conversational sense ('great!, excellent!') (as a one-word reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sound', forming an aspectual pair with 'прозвучать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (to be heard) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот теперь звучит как настоящий мэр!
examples.trans: Now that sounds like a real mayor!

examples.text: Это звучит очень странно и подозрительно.
examples.trans: That sounds very strange and suspicious.

examples.text: Разве это не звучит великолепно для гостей?
examples.trans: Does that not sound magnificent for the guests?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'logical' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'веча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'candle' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.
Candles are burning on the table.

examples.text: Прекрасно! Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: Wonderful! I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'magic' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Там великолепный вид и совершенно волшебная атмосфера.
examples.trans: There is a magnificent view and completely magical atmosphere.
